key_insight: Thermal history, along with composition, controls hidden nanoscale octahedral-tilt disorder in lead halide perovskites, which in turn alters their optoelectronic response.
engineering_relevance: Processing conditions such as heating rate and phase-transition path should be treated as design variables for perovskite devices because they can change local structure and photoluminescence efficiency during fabrication and operation.
method: Single-crystal X-ray and neutron diffuse scattering across Cs/MA/FA, Cl/Br/I, and mixed-halide perovskites
Machine-learning-assisted molecular dynamics plus a phenomenological octahedral-tilt model to map local dynamic nanodomains
Hyperspectral photoluminescence to connect structural history with optoelectronic response
evidence_signal: The study combines diffuse scattering, modeling, and photoluminescence across accessible phases and reports that heating rate alone changes photoluminescence quantum efficiency in MAPbI3.
watch_item: Thermal-history effects are composition- and phase-dependent, so results may not transfer directly without controlling ramp rate, phase transitions, and measurement conditions.
paper_title: Thermal history controls the optoelectronic response of lead halide perovskites through structure and dynamics
